ai.description: This lizard reaches 45 cm in length. It is bright green with dark crossbands and a prominent, serrated dorsal crest. Large, keeled scales cover the body, distinguishing it from other *Calotes* species.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable cue for *Calotes grandisquamis* is the presence of a distinct, black-bordered, pale-yellow or white patch located just above the shoulder (the axilla).
ai.habitat: The Large-scaled Forest Lizard inhabits the evergreen and semi-evergreen rainforests of the Western Ghats, typically at elevations between 600 and 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Large-scaled Forest Lizard is primarily diurnal, often seen basking on tree trunks or branches to regulate its body temperature before actively hunting for insects.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Calotes grandisquamis* is oviparous, laying clutches of 6–10 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, spanning from June to September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Calotes grandisquamis* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats of India, primarily occurring in Kerala and Tamil Nadu at elevations between 600 and 1,600 meters.
